title: Champion Architecture Lessons (TCH/Cairn Retrospective)
description: Two-layer blackboard+DAG scheduling, minimal protocol, parallel homogeneous workers, full-speed use of the strongest models
detail:
Core practices from a retrospective on a team that fully completed all 54 targets in a past authorized assessment exercise:
1. Only two layers: a scheduling layer (blackboard + DAG engine, i.e., the fact graph) + an execution layer (Claude Code / Codex used directly as atomic workers)
2. Avoid splitting agents by penetration-testing phases (recon/exploitation/post-exploitation roles) — in exploratory work, paths emerge through interaction; splitting roles imposes human constraints on the model. The correct use of multiple agents is parallel compute: homogeneous workers exploring different branches
3. Minimal environment: a Kali container equipped with tools + a single proof-artifact submission skill; no MCP, no RAG, no predefined workflow (generic skills can cap the ceiling)
4. Run the strongest models at full speed (Opus+GPT; 5 days, 7692 CNY / 1.09 billion tokens). Early low concurrency was a mistake that limited ranking despite full completion — under dynamic scoring, speed equals points
5. Preserve structured logs; when stuck, a human review of logs injected with intent was the final turning point
Source: https://l3yx.github.io (TCH retrospective + harness engineering evolution)
